sentences.text: Spatulidentatus reached roughly 2.7 m in total length, placing it in the medium-sized range for sauropterygians.
Its skull was notably small at 13.3 cm, about five percent of the animal’s overall length.
The teeth were spoon-shaped, with a narrowed neck and flattened, expanded crowns that curved toward the tongue.
The tail comprised at least 58 vertebrae and accounted for roughly 42 % of the body length.
Both back and tail vertebrae featured unusually long neural spines.
The humerus displayed a pronounced widening at its distal end and a well-developed condyle.
The front limbs were comparatively longer and sturdier than the rear limbs.
The genus and species were formally named in 2026 by Mei Yang and colleagues.
The holotype, specimen GMG10, resides permanently in the Geological Museum of Guizhou.
Although no formal phylogenetic analysis was conducted, its anatomy suggests a basal, early-diverging position among sauropterygians.
Features such as a short snout, triangular maxilla, and a robust lower jaw link it to early European sauropterygians like Paraplacodus and Eusaurosphargis.
Spatulidentatus breviceps is the type species of its genus.
It lived during the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
